subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find an algebraic equation of degree 4 whose roots are 3 times the roots of the equation 6x⁴ − 7x³ + 8x² − 7x + 2 = 0.

mark_split.label: Multiply by 3⁴ and write the equation

recall_prompt: Say what you replace x by, and how you clear the fractions afterwards.
insider_note: Each coefficient is multiplied by a power of 3 that grows as the degree falls: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Replace x by x/3
steps.margin_note: First mark. New roots 3α ⇒ α = x/3, so the required equation is f(x/3) = 0. Denominators 81, 27, 9, 3.

recall.must_convey: That the equation whose roots are three times the old ones is f(x/3) = 0, obtained by replacing x by x/3.
accept: replace x by x by three because the new root is three times the old one
the required equation is f of x by three equals zero
put x over three in place of x
x place lo x by three pettali, f of x by three equals zero
roots tripled means substitute x over three

steps.why: If f(α) = 0 then f((3α)/3) = 0, so 3α is a root of f(x/3) = 0. Tripling the roots means dividing the variable by 3.
common_mistakes: Replacing x by 3x, which divides the roots by 3 instead.
Forgetting to raise the 3 to the power along with x: (x/3)⁴ = x⁴/81.

steps.label: Multiply by 3⁴

recall.must_convey: That multiplying by 3⁴ = 81 clears the fractions and gives 6x⁴ − 21x³ + 72x² − 189x + 162 = 0.
accept: multiply by eighty one and the equation is six x four minus twenty one x cube plus seventy two x square minus one eighty nine x plus one sixty two
clear the denominators with three to the four
the answer is six x to the four minus twenty one x cubed plus seventy two x squared minus one hundred eighty nine x plus one hundred sixty two
eighty one tho multiply chesthe six x four minus twenty one x cube plus seventy two x square minus one eighty nine x plus one sixty two
multiply through by three to the power four

steps.why: Multiplying by 81 does not change the roots and gives integer coefficients. Each coefficient of the original is multiplied by 3 to the power of (4 − its degree): 1, 3, 9, 27, 81.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the constant 2 by 1 instead of 81.
A slip such as 7 × 27 = 189 written as 179.
